_comment: Why this file exists. stop_reason is a published enumeration under Rule 6 — it
appears on every TaskRecord and every `turn` audit record, and a consumer
switches on it. It was pinned only by a hand-kept list inside docs.test.ts,
which checked one direction: a value documented in CONTRACTS.md but never
emitted by the code would have passed, and so would a value the code emits
that nobody documented. Both are drift.
This fixture is the third point that makes the check two-way. The test asserts
the union in prompt_loop.ts, the table in docs/CONTRACTS.md, and the keys here
are the SAME SET — so adding a value means touching all three deliberately,
the same shape as conformance/exit_codes.json.
`truncated` was added 2026-09-05, found by benchmarks/degradation-contract: a
reply the backend cut off twice was allowed to stand and recorded as
`answered`.
`malformed` was added 2026-09-29: replies with no usable tool call (invalid
arguments, an unknown tool, markup in place of a call, or a call the endpoint
could not parse) were re-asked with no bound but the step wall, or -- for
markup -- once, and then recorded as `answered`.
`in_progress` and `killed` were added 2026-11-04 (C5): a run killed mid-turn --
a benchmark's time cap -- left no record at all. The live record
(<session>.record.json, docs/CONTRACTS.md §28) writes them; no turn returns them.
`endpoint_error` was added 2026-11-05 (P2G41 acid test): a turn that ended because its
last model request failed -- code 12 after the transport grace, in three cells -- was
recorded as `answered`, one of them with no tool step at all.
`deadline` was added 2026-11-05 (TB1, P2G41): `gnomon task --deadline` stops the
turn itself before an external time cap, with a final record and a sealed trail;
Harbor never signals the process it runs, so 29 of 29 capped cells left only a
partial record.

stop_reason.answered: the model stopped calling tools of its own accord
stop_reason.empty: the model returned neither text nor a tool call
stop_reason.stall: the same call repeated until the stall limit
stop_reason.truncated: the backend cut the reply off at its output limit, and the bounded re-asks did not finish it: a cut text reply stands as the answer (a result); cut tool calls in a row end on the refusal floor with stop_detail.repeats
stop_reason.apparatus: the run never reached the model — the surface itself could not be used
stop_reason.malformed: replies in a row offered no usable tool call, past [turn] max_consecutive_malformed repair turns
stop_reason.endpoint_error: the turn's last model request failed and the turn ended on it: no key (10), no reply in time (11), the provider unreachable or erroring past the transport grace (12), or the context could not be fitted (13); the code says which, and the bucket is apparatus_failure
stop_reason.tamper: a tool call, or something between calls, changed gnomon's own records and gnomon did not make the change; the turn stops with a refusal (3) and a record_tamper record
stop_reason.in_progress: the turn had not ended when the record was written; only on a partial record (record_state: partial), which is what a SIGKILL leaves
stop_reason.killed: SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP ended the process mid-turn and the record was flushed first; stop_detail.signal names the signal, and the record is apparatus_failure (11)
stop_reason.deadline: gnomon task --deadline (or GNOMON_DEADLINE) was given and the turn reached the deadline less its margin, so it stopped itself: the call in flight aborted, the record final, the trail sealed; on the refusal floor a step_wall lands on (exit 2), with stop_detail.deadline, budget_ms and margin_ms

not_a_bucket: stop_reason is a separate axis from the outcome bucket. The bucket says WHAT happened; this says why the loop stopped. Nothing here maps to result/refusal/apparatus_failure, and a reader combining them is producing a composite verdict this project refuses to publish.
